correctness.rationale: For every unselected edge uv, deg_F(u)+deg_F(v)=1. The degree trichotomy and two coordinate-square contradictions exclude selected yellow–yellow edges and any nontrivial selected black–black edge. Connected bipartition then forces the yellow side to equal a parity class, each with exactly one black neighbor; counting gives d|2^(d-1), |F|=2^(d-1). Explicit even-parity zero-syndrome vectors give a one-sided perfect code in every dimension 2^r. Q2/Q3 exhaustive and Q4 code enumeration plus Q8 construction replayed from included verifier. Finite tests are only supplementary.

value.rationale: A natural symmetric graph family undergoes a sharp, infinite sequence of dimension-dependent changes: in non-dyadic dimensions the only PEDS is the entire edge set, whereas in dyadic dimensions optimal PEDS occupy only one d-th of the edges. The bijection with one-sided binary perfect codes proves all configurations structurally, going substantively beyond the generic black/yellow/white coloring or finite benchmark tables.
